A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and provide readable text, equations, analytical examples, and complete proofs. All pages were inspected. Neither version contains a separately labeled appendix, figure, or table.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical convergence results, analytically calculated Examples 1–3, and proofs in Section 4. It contains no original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: v3 remains theoretical, retaining the analytical examples and presenting proofs in Section 5. Its added discussion and revised mathematics introduce no empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The binary and multiclass cubic-partition classifiers, cell statistics, and cellwise Laplace privatization mechanism remain unchanged. The revised bandwidth requirements concern theoretical guarantees rather than a new algorithmic procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets for training or empirical evaluation. Binary and multiclass classification with observable and privatized data remain the theoretical settings, and Examples 1–3 retain their distributions.

E2.justification: Neither version evaluates empirical baselines. Comparisons with earlier theoretical rates remain; the newly cited federated-learning and XGBoost papers are contextual references, not evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: There are no experimental protocols, splits, training budgets, or evaluation procedures in either version. The added bandwidth restrictions are mathematical assumptions for convergence results.

E4.justification: The three analytical examples illustrating failure of the strong density assumption are retained. No ablations, robustness experiments, sensitivity studies, or additional case studies are introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, confidence intervals, or empirical significance tests. CLT and Berry–Esséen arguments remain theoretical proof tools rather than uncertainty reporting for experiments.

E6.justification: Examples 1–3 retain their explicit calculated rates, including n^(-2/3), n^(-(2+delta)/3) in the stated parameter range, and n^(-8/15). No empirical result entries are added or revised; changes to general mathematical bounds are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorems 3.1–3.2 now require both original and modified margin-density conditions, retain a separate sampling-error term omitted from v2's final private bounds, and revise the privacy-error exponent. Theorem 3.1 adds a bandwidth restriction for its simplified rate. Lemma 4.1 becomes Lemma 5.1 with ordered posterior gaps, a gap/2 threshold replacing gap/M, and a supplied proof; subsequent multiclass derivations change accordingly. Theorems also explicitly require monotonically vanishing bandwidths.

C1.justification: Both abstracts and introductions retain the central contributions: fast binary and multiclass partitioning rates without the strong density assumption, intrinsic-dimensional dependence, and extensions to local differential privacy. The new Discussion largely restates these headline contributions.

C2.justification: v2's assertion ordering the nonprivate and private density exponents, together with its dominance illustration after Theorem 3.1, is removed. v3 states conditions for simplifying the private bound and adds discussion of the privacy-related slowdown and relevance to broader learning methods.

D1.justification: The Laplace noise specification and calibration sigma_Z = 2sqrt(2)/alpha are retained. Neither version supplies experimental implementation details, hardware information, or code/data access instructions.

R1.justification: v3 adds four works: Argente-Garrido et al. on federated decision-tree aggregation, Chen and Guestrin on XGBoost, and two Györfi–Kroll papers on private density estimation and regression. These expand application context and connect the retained privacy mechanism to related estimation problems.

P1.justification: v3 edits the abstract, expands introductory motivation, adds Discussion and Acknowledgements before the proofs, and simplifies density-exponent notation to gamma_1 and gamma_2. The overall progression from observable classification to private classification and proofs remains.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted: page proportions and margins change, section headings become standalone, title and author typography are redesigned, running author headers appear, and equation numbers move from left to right. Neither version contains figures or tables.

improvement.justification: v3 improves transparency by retaining sampling error in the private bounds and explicitly qualifying when the simplified rate follows. The supplied multiclass lemma proof and new discussion improve checkability and exposition. These gains are moderated by new inconsistencies, including Theorem 3.2 citing binary conditions (3) and (9) instead of their multiclass counterparts, supporting a limited overall improvement.
